rules.statement: Illegitimate children who are publicly acknowledged by their father or born in his house under circumstances showing an act of open recognition of cohabitation with their mother may inherit their father's acquired property, but only if there are no legitimate children and no widow.
rules.supporting_quote: "The illegitimate children referred to at p. 71 may of course be the offspring of what Armour terms an unlawful marriage. I think therefore the rule enunciated by Lawrie, J., 2 S.C.R., p. 134, although the question then affected movables only, is good, but might be enlarged to the extent of saying that where there are no legitimate children and no widow, purely illegitimate children publicly acknowledged by their father or born in bis house, under circumstances showing an open acknowledgment of the existence of cohabitation with their mother, succeed to the purchased or acquired property of their father."
